## What is an ordered sequence?

`ordered_sequence` stores elements sorted by key, with stable FIFO behavior for
duplicate keys.

```{r}
xs <- ordered_sequence("a1", "b1", "b2", "c1", keys = c(1, 2, 2, 3))
xs
```

`as_flexseq(xs)` returns a payload-only `flexseq`; keys and any custom
monoids are dropped.

## Key-based lookup

```{r}
peek_key(xs, 2)
as.list(peek_all_key(xs, 2))
count_key(xs, 2)
```

## Key boundaries

`lower_bound()` gives first `>= key`, and `upper_bound()` gives first `> key`.

```{r}
lower_bound(xs, 2)
upper_bound(xs, 2)
```

## Key range queries

```{r}
elements_between(xs, 2, 3)
count_between(xs, 2, 3)
count_between(xs, 2, 3, include_to = FALSE)
```

## Pop by key

```{r}
one <- pop_key(xs, 2)
one$value
one$key
one$remaining

all_two <- pop_all_key(xs, 2)
as.list(all_two$values)
all_two$remaining
```

## Insert

```{r}
xs2 <- insert(xs, "a2", key = 1)
xs2
```
